sources.supports: A wound mainspring supplies motive force; the escapement uses the balance, pallet fork, and escape wheel to regulate gear motion; the balance carries a hairspring; the gear train drives the hands.
sources.limits: The page describes Grand Seiko 9S movements, whose construction varies by caliber. The 4 Hz teaching rate appears for specific listed calibers, not every mechanical watch. Schematic geometry, state counters, and ideal timing here are not a specific 9S movement.

sources.supports: Seiko describes a typical quartz watch using a battery, a quartz reference near 32,768 oscillations per second, electronic division to a one-second signal, a step motor, and gears.
sources.limits: The Japanese educational page says 32,768 Hz is typical and explicitly notes exceptions. It is a general explanation, not a specification for every quartz watch.

sources.supports: Grand Seiko describes the 9F battery, quartz oscillator, integrated circuit, step motor, gears, and hands; its 9F twin-pulse motor sends two second-hand steps per second.
sources.limits: This describes the specific Grand Seiko 9F movement. The generic model uses one motor command per second; it does not claim the 9F pulse pattern or universal quartz motor behavior.

sources.supports: KHK gives gear ratio magnitude in terms of tooth counts and rotational speeds and distinguishes rotation directions for internal gear arrangements.
sources.limits: This is general gear-design information, not a watch-specific tooth count or validation of a particular watch train. The schematic labels do not assert a real watch gear geometry.

sources.supports: requestAnimationFrame schedules rendering callbacks, normally follows display refresh, and is paused in most hidden tabs.
sources.limits: Callback timing is a browser scheduling observation, not a logical software-watch tick. This component model does not count callbacks or claim callback timing accuracy.

sources.supports: A fixed logical update is kept separate from render cadence; elapsed time can be accumulated to decide when updates are due.
sources.limits: This source motivates the teaching separation only. It does not specify this app’s runtime policy or prove physical watch timing.

components.name: Crown and winding input
components.formula: No winding action or stored-energy amount is simulated; energy is controlled by the explicit teaching-model energy toggle.

components.name: Barrel
components.formula: The current boolean says whether the modeled mainspring energy path is available; it is not a reserve measurement.

components.name: Mainspring
components.formula: Reads the modeled energy-enabled state. Stored torque, energy, and power reserve are not simulated.

components.name: Going and hand gear train
components.formula: Reads derived hand turns, teaching gear-pair ratios, and hand angles for the configured elapsed display time. Tooth counts are teaching choices, not a named watch train.

components.name: Escape wheel
components.formula: The model records its controlled escapement event index; the index does not simulate tooth contact geometry.

components.name: Pallet fork
components.formula: Reads the discrete modeled escapement phase (lock, release, or impulse); it is an ideal teaching sequence.

components.name: Balance wheel
components.formula: Counts modeled full balance oscillations. A full oscillation contains two escapement beats.

components.name: Hairspring
components.formula: Reads the same ideal oscillator phase used by the balance model; it does not model spring shape, torque, or material behavior.

components.name: Plate, bridges, pivots, and jewels
components.formula: Support geometry is illustrative and has no dynamic state in this teaching model.

components.name: Second hand
components.formula: Angle = 360 × (nominal display time / hand period) modulo 360; second period 60 s, minute period 3,600 s, hour period 43,200 s. Later oscillator-rate changes alter when visible events occur and cause modeled drift.

components.name: Battery

components.name: Quartz resonator
components.formula: Reads the exact modeled reference-cycle counter. The 32,768 Hz setting is a generic teaching parameter, not a universal watch specification.

components.name: Oscillator circuit
components.formula: Reads the modeled oscillator phase; this is not an electrical waveform or circuit-level simulation.

components.name: Frequency divider
components.formula: Each listed stage divides by two; the standard example uses fifteen stages from 32,768 Hz to 1 Hz.

components.name: Motor driver
components.formula: Counts generic one-per-second motor commands. A command is not a universal electrical pulse pattern.

components.name: Coil and stator
components.formula: The schematic separates a generic motor drive from its count; coil current and magnetic fields are not simulated.

components.name: Step-motor rotor
components.formula: Shows the motor-command count as a teaching proxy; it does not claim a universal rotor angle or pulse-to-step ratio.

components.name: Reduction and display gears
